summary: Okta device-authenticator challenge blocking access to internal admin consoles after MFA policy update
steps_to_reproduce: User with corporate laptop (managed by Intune) attempts to access /admin/console
Okta prompts for device authenticator challenge after recent MFA policy change
User completes challenge, but Okta returns error IDX10311 and does not issue session cookie
Access denied in Redwood Console with 403 / 'insufficient_scope' in frontend logs
Reproduced for 3 different users across 2 teams (Platform, Solutions)
logs: Okta auth log excerpt: 2026-03-10T08:12:41Z - user: j.tan - transaction.id=abc123 - factor.challenge - error=IDX10311
Redwood API gateway: 2026-03-10T08:12:43Z - GET /admin/console - 403 - x-request-id=rr-9f3 - reason=insufficient_scope
investigation_notes: After the MFA policy rollout at 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC, ~6% of corporate devices started failing the device-authenticator challenge. Error IDX10311 indicates Okta declined the device assertion. SCIM group mapping and RBAC appear unchanged. Early hypothesis: new policy enforcement expects a device claim (deviceId) that some managed devices are not sending due to Intune/endpoint config mismatch. Also observed failing sessions are coming from the corp vpn egress IPs; possible timing/session cookie handshake issue with our session cookie domain after Okta's response changed.
comments: Maya Patel (Reporter) 2026-03-10: Noticed multiple Platform engineers cannot access admin routes after this morning's MFA policy update. They get the Okta challenge and then 403 on console. Filing now.

Daniel Ortega (Assignee) 2026-03-10: Investigating. First-pass: pulling Okta System Logs and cross-checking with Splunk traces for affected x-request-ids. Asked IT-Sec to confirm whether any device attestation changes were pushed to Intune last night.

IT-Security (Elena Ruiz) 2026-03-11: Confirmed a micro-update to the endpoint attestation agent was rolled to ~40% of corp-managed laptops at 2026-03-09 21:40 UTC. Rolling it back on a canary set now.

SRE (Jordan Li) 2026-03-11: Observed cookie mismatch when Okta returns a challenge response with missing device claim; session not persisted by our gateway. Temporary mitigation: bypass device challenge check for sessions coming from internal VPN for ivy.redwood-internal domain until root cause fixed.
Daniel Ortega 2026-03-12: Applied temporary policy override in Okta to allow 'require device' exceptions for corp-vpn network. Monitoring for 24h.
Maya Patel 2026-03-13: Confirmed access restored for previously affected users. Keeping ticket open until we have a durable fix and run SCIM sync.
resolution: Partial mitigation implemented: temporary Okta policy exception for corp VPN traffic and rollback of the endpoint attestation agent on canary cohort. Next steps: (1) Coordinate with IT to ensure attestation agent includes deviceId claim for all managed devices; (2) Run full SCIM group sync and validate RBAC mappings; (3) Remove policy exception and re-run canary. Owners: identity-team, it-security. Target for full resolution: 2026-03-15.
notes_for_followup: Run a scheduled job to verify device claim presence in Okta logs for all managed devices for three consecutive days. Add a runbook entry for device-authenticator failures and include a quick override playbook for on-call.
